name: Rejuvenex Inj.

lead: Rejuvenex is a brand of PDRN, a mixture of DNA fragments purified from salmon (Oncorhynchus keta) sperm, delivered by injection in clinics. It is used in skin-rejuvenation treatments to improve texture, hydration and healing.

PDRN is thought to act on adenosine A2A receptors and the nucleotide salvage pathway, which supports cell growth, collagen production and calming of inflammation. Published work on Rejuvenex is mostly mouse wound-healing and cell-culture research.

paras: It is administered by clinicians as small skin injections, often within rejuvenation or post-procedure recovery programs; in Asia PDRN is commonly used after laser or microneedling. Practitioners describe courses of sessions with gradual change.

Injectable procedures carry general risks such as bruising, swelling and infection. The product is derived from fish material, which matters for people with fish allergies. Human cosmetic trials are limited.

angle.text: Clinics inject PDRN to support skin repair and collagen, aiming for smoother, more resilient skin and faster recovery after resurfacing procedures. The pathway is supported by cell and animal research.

lead: Rejuvenex Inj. is a polydeoxyribonucleotide (PDRN) injectable derived from the sperm of the chum salmon Oncorhynchus keta, sold alongside a cream version and used for skin repair and rejuvenation.[1] PDRN itself is a mixture of single-stranded DNA fragments; it was first isolated from human placenta in Italy and is now mostly made from salmon or trout DNA.[2]

PDRN is thought to act by activating adenosine A2A receptors, raising cAMP and signalling that increases growth factors such as VEGF, and by feeding the nucleotide salvage pathway that supports cell proliferation. It is described as anti-inflammatory and as stimulating collagen and new blood vessels.[2] In Asia it is commonly used as a biostimulator after procedures like laser treatment or microneedling.[2]

Published research on Rejuvenex specifically is a mouse wound-healing study comparing it with another PDRN product, and laboratory research on PDRN alternatives that uses it as a commercial comparator.[1][3]

paras: Rejuvenex is a PDRN medication extracted from O. keta, available as an injection and as Rejuvenex Cream.[1] Related commercial PDRN products include Placentex (from O. mykiss) and HiDr.[3]

Enzymatic breakdown of PDRN activates adenosine A2A receptors, increasing cAMP and PKA activity and upregulating PI3K/Akt and VEGF; it also supplies building blocks to the salvage pathway of DNA synthesis.[2] Researchers describe wound-healing and anti-inflammatory activity.[1][3]

No human studies found specific to Rejuvenex in the reviewed sources. A mouse study with 60 animals compared O. keta-derived PDRN injection (Rejuvenex) and cream with an O. mykiss-derived injection and saline: the injection groups showed the greatest wound-healing effect and similar scores to each other.[1] A 2023 cell study of a red-algae PDRN found anti-inflammatory activity and increased collagen production in human dermal fibroblasts, using commercial PDRN products for comparison.[3]

Commercial PDRN is extracted from fish sperm, which is expensive and seasonal, which led researchers to explore plant and algal alternatives.[3] Standard injection risks apply, and the material is of animal origin.
